definitions.explanation: To take something that belongs to someone else without permission.

examples.japanese: ⟦{財布|さいふ}→財布：00663_saifu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{盗|ぬす}まれた。
examples.notes: Passive form is common for victims

examples.japanese: ⟦{泥棒|どろぼう}→泥棒：01688_dorobou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宝石|ほうせき}→宝石：03619_houseki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{盗|ぬす}んだ。
⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{盗|ぬす}んではいけない。
examples.english: You must not steal other people's things.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{盗|ぬす}む (steal X).

ASPECT: ている indicates completed action. {盗|ぬす}んでいる = 'has stolen.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{物|もの}を{盗|ぬす}む (steal things)
・{盗|ぬす}まれる (be stolen—passive, very common)
・こっそり{盗|ぬす}む (steal stealthily)
・{盗|ぬす}み{見|み}る (peep, peek)
・{盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}き (eavesdropping)

RELATED:
・{泥棒|どろぼう} (thief, burglar)
・{窃盗|せっとう} (theft—formal/legal term)
・{盗難|とうなん} (theft, robbery—noun)

PASSIVE USAGE: Victims often use the passive {盗|ぬす}まれる to describe their experience:
・{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{盗|ぬす}まれた (My bicycle was stolen)
